text:
maria_cs: ParcelPro reporting: after today's rollout their ingest validator is failing. They say order IDs now have an added prefix and their strict schema rejects them. Ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-6128

parcelpro_cust: Hi team — after the flip to model v3.1 we started getting validation errors. Example payload and the validator error are below. This worked yesterday.

parcelpro_cust: ```
Request: POST /v1/generate
{
  "prompt": "serialize order as json",
  "model": "redwood-instruct-3.1"
}

Response (excerpt):
{
  "order_id": "meta>ORD-92384",
  "items": [ { "sku": "ABC123", "qty": 2 } ]
}

Validator error:
E: order_id does not match pattern ^ORD-[0-9]+$ (found "meta>ORD-92384")
```

maria_cs: They say they enforce the regex for order_id and now it fails on ~15% of requests. Started right after deploy at 10:07 UTC.

alex_eng: thanks — tagging runtime and deploy. @sam_runtime can you check whether any output post-processing added a prefix for certain tokenization edge cases? :eyes:

sam_runtime: looking. Deploy bot shows canary -> v3.1 rolled to 30% at 10:05, 100% at 10:09 per the rollout logs. deploy-bot: ```Canary update: redwood-instruct v3.1 promoted to stable at 2026-03-17T10:09:12Z```

sam_runtime: quick hypothesis: our structured-output normalizer has a new rule intended to tag ambiguous IDs with source hints (adds `meta>` for tokens that start with a letter then dash). I need sample from logs where generation returned prefix. @alex_eng can you share request ids from customer?

jordan_support: ParcelPro provided request ids in the ticket: r-29834, r-29857, r-29904. They included raw responses.

alex_eng: pasted their raw response for r-29857 into the thread (above). Looks like prefix is inserted before the ORD- token. Not everything is affected — some responses remain plain ORD-...

sam_runtime: reproducing locally with redwood-instruct-3.1 on CPU using their prompt. Repro steps I used:
1) curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"serialize order as json","model":"redwood-instruct-3.1"}'
2) capture output and parse as json

Result: I see both `\"ORD-98421\"` and `\"meta>ORD-92384\"` depending on sampling seed. Seed deterministic run: with seed=42 got meta> prefix.

sam_runtime: stack trace points to structured normalizer layer call normalize_ids(output, context) which applies:
```python
def normalize_ids(obj):
  if looks_ambiguous(obj["order_id"]):
    return f"meta>{obj["order_id"]}"
  return obj["order_id"]
```
This rule was introduced in PR #4123 to help downstream log parsing, but it wasn't gated behind the canary flag. Oops.

alex_eng: that explains intermittent nature. ParcelPro's validator is strict so any prefix breaks them. We should revert or gate the change.

sam_runtime: plan: revert PR on runtime side and cut hotfix canary restoring previous behavior. I'll coordinate with deploy.

deploy-bot: ```Revert request created: revert-runtime-pr-4123 by sam_runtime. Hotfix branch: hotfix/normalize-ids-revert.```

maria_cs: Jordan — please give ParcelPro ETA and mitigation steps. Also ask if they can accept a tolerant regex temporarily (we can provide examples).

jordan_support: On it. Messaging now: "We're aware of a regression introduced by today's model runtime change adding a 'meta>' prefix to some order_id values. Engineering has a hotfix in progress and expects a staged revert within 30-45 minutes. As a temporary workaround, you can relax the regex to accept an optional meta> prefix: ^(meta>)?ORD-[0-9]+$." :thumbsup:

parcelpro_cust: Thanks — we'll update validator temporarily and monitor. Can you confirm whether any historical data was affected?

sam_runtime: looking at logs since 10:05 UTC — ~2.3k responses; about 14% contain the prefix. All are request-scoped (not persisted by us) so only their downstream ingest would be impacted. No database changes on our side.

alex_eng: filing follow-up to add integration test that validates structured-output transforms don't mutate schema-bound fields unless explicitly enabled. Also add rollout gating for runtime flags.

maria_cs: thx team. I'll mark ticket CS-6128 as engineering-assigned and update customer with the revert timeline and validation workaround. :white_check_mark:
